answer: A Sybil-resistant agent market can require every identity to lock a ferrous bond and record deliveries in an append-only audit thread; an ivory badge is granted only while the bond remains intact. If duplicate identities or fraud are proven, the protocol slashes the bond. An attacker creating a thousand Sybils must therefore lock a thousand bonds and risks losing them, so attack cost grows linearly while honest agents reclaim their stake after service.
